name: Kerguelen Islands (French Southern Lands reserve)
blurb: Penguins, seals and albatrosses, plus rabbits and cats that reshaped the land.

tip.title: Remove the feral cats
tip.text: Set Feral cat to -100%. Rabbits lose a predator and rise, so Kerguelen cabbage, cushion plants and tussock are grazed harder, while king penguins lose a predator too.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Short, cool, often cloudy summers limit how much light reaches the plants and plankton that start the food web.

nodes.name: Antarctic Convergence
nodes.desc: The Southern Ocean boundary where cold and warmer waters meet, which concentrates plankton and the fish and squid that feed on it.

nodes.name: Wet, windswept soil
nodes.desc: Kerguelen cabbage grows where soil water stays high, in a climate with constant wind.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Microbes and soil invertebrates break down dead plants, carcasses and seabird waste, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Kerguelen cabbage
nodes.desc: Edible cabbage-like plant of subantarctic islands. Introduced rabbits eat it, so it now survives mainly where rabbits cannot reach.

nodes.name: Cushion azorella
nodes.desc: Compact cushion plant common in the islands fellfield and rocky ground, and eaten by introduced rabbits.

nodes.name: Cook's tussock grass
nodes.desc: Tussock grass of subantarctic coasts and slopes. Introduced rabbits graze it.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting microscopic algae of the surrounding Southern Ocean, the base of the marine food web.

nodes.name: European rabbit
nodes.desc: Introduced around 1874. It grazes cabbage, cushion plants and grasses, and is prey for feral cats and skuas.

nodes.name: Kerguelen flightless moth
nodes.desc: Flightless moth whose larvae feed on Kerguelen cabbage, a major part of the native litter-feeding fauna.

nodes.name: Lanternfish
nodes.desc: Small, abundant deep-sea fish that rise toward the surface at night and are the staple food of king penguins and many other predators.

nodes.name: Krill and zooplankton
nodes.desc: Small shrimp-like crustaceans that graze phytoplankton and feed fish, penguins and seabirds.

nodes.name: Feral cat
nodes.desc: Descended from ships cats. They hunt rabbits, mice and nesting seabirds, including penguins, on land.

nodes.name: Brown skua
nodes.desc: Predator, pirate and scavenger: takes penguin chicks, eggs, seabirds, rabbits, fish and carrion.

nodes.name: Southern giant petrel
nodes.desc: Large petrel that kills penguin chicks and seabirds and scavenges carrion, notably from elephant seals.

nodes.name: King penguin
nodes.desc: Breeds in large colonies at Kerguelen, about 240,000 to 280,000 pairs. Eats mostly lanternfish and squid.

nodes.name: Gentoo penguin
nodes.desc: Penguin of subantarctic coasts that feeds on fish and crustaceans such as krill, and is hunted by leopard seals and orcas.

nodes.name: Black-browed albatross
nodes.desc: Albatross that breeds at Kerguelen and eats fish, squid, crustaceans, carrion and fishery discards.

nodes.name: Antarctic fur seal
nodes.desc: At Kerguelen it feeds mostly on fish and squid rather than krill, and its numbers there are growing.

nodes.name: Southern elephant seal
nodes.desc: Dives deep for squid and fish. Kerguelen holds about three-quarters of the Indian Ocean breeding population.

nodes.name: Leopard seal
nodes.desc: Predator of penguins and young seals, recorded killing weaned elephant seal pups.

nodes.name: Orca
nodes.desc: Top marine predator that hunts penguins, seals and large whales.
